name: Hotwind Youth Club
tagline: A little curiosity. A lot of possibility.
从一点好奇，走向更多可能。
intro: A student-led community where reading opens conversations, people find their voice, and ideas become shared experiences.
一个由青年共同建设的社群：让阅读开启对话，让每个人被听见，让想法成为共同经历。

label: activities organised
场线上线下活动
note: Across reading, dialogue and health communication
涵盖阅读、对话与健康传播

label: weeks of shared reading
周线上共读计划
note: A sustained space for learning together
持续陪伴的朋辈学习空间

label: people in the core team
位核心团队成员
note: A small team with shared responsibilities
共同分工、共同建设的小团队

title: Start with a reading salon
从一场读书沙龙开始
text: I started Hotwind for university students who wanted a more open, sincere place to read, exchange ideas and connect beyond formal coursework.
我发起热風，希望为大学生创造一个更开放、真诚的空间，在课程之外一起阅读、交换想法、建立连接。
lesson: Begin with a need you can see.
从身边真实的需求出发。

title: Test a bigger idea
试验更大的可能
text: An innovation project became a way to explore the relationship between reading, peer support and youth development.
通过创新项目，我们开始探索阅读、朋辈支持与青年成长之间的联系。
lesson: An early idea is something to test.
最初的想法，需要在实践中检验。

title: Reflect, then rebuild
反思边界，重新搭建
text: Recognising the limits of student-led psychological support, we repositioned the community around dialogue, learning and public engagement, and rebuilt the team around this direction.
认识到学生主导心理支持的专业边界后，我们把方向重新聚焦于对话、学习与公众参与，并围绕新的定位重建团队。
lesson: 倾听，也意味着愿意调整方向。

title: Become a connector
从组织活动，到连接青年
text: The community connected students with academic, cultural, public-interest and life-science communities across Chongqing and Wuhan.
社群逐步连接重庆、武汉的学术、文化、公益与生命科学社群，为青年打开更多交流与探索的入口。
lesson: 让共同关心的问题，成为连接的起点。

label: READING & CONNECTION
阅读与连接
title: Read together. Think further.
一起读，也一起想得更远。
summary: A small reading salon and a 20-week online programme made shared learning a regular part of community life.
从小型读书沙龙到20周线上共读，让共同学习成为社群生活的一部分。
question: What if reading were a starting point for connection?
如果阅读，也能成为人与人连接的起点？
why: I wanted a place where students could exchange ideas beyond coursework and have conversations with enough time and trust to go deeper.
我希望大家在课程之外也能交换想法，在有时间、有信任的交流中，把一个问题讨论得更深入。

title: Start small
小规模开始
text: Reading salons created a manageable setting for students to share interpretations and questions.
通过小型读书沙龙，让参与者分享理解、提出疑问。

title: Keep showing up
让交流持续发生
text: An online shared-reading programme continued for around 20 weeks.
组织持续约20周的线上共读计划。

title: Let ideas travel
让想法延伸
text: Reading became an entry point to wider conversations about society, personal growth and public life.
从书中的内容出发，延伸到社会、个人成长与公共生活。

role: I founded the community and coordinated its development with the core team, helping turn informal interest into a recurring programme.
我发起社群，与核心团队共同协调发展，把最初的阅读兴趣逐步转化为持续开展的活动。
reflection: Continuity can matter as much as scale: a recurring invitation gives people more than one chance to take part.
持续性与规模同样重要：一次次发出邀请，让参与者有机会慢慢融入。

label: PLAY & PUBLIC HEALTH
游戏与公共健康
title: A mystery that starts a conversation.
让一个谜题，开启健康对话。
summary: An original medical mystery, a diagnostic social game and a short science talk offered an interactive way into tuberculosis awareness.
将原创医学剧本、诊断主题社交游戏与简短科普结合，为结核病知识提供有参与感的入口。
question: How could health education invite people to participate?
怎样让健康科普，更愿意被主动参与？
why: Tuberculosis is a medical topic, but the activity needed an accessible starting point for participants without specialist knowledge. A mystery provided a shared question to explore.
结核病是医学议题，但活动需要让没有专业背景的参与者也能进入。一个共同破解的谜题，为探索提供了起点。

title: Enter the story
进入故事
text: An original medical mystery introduced a shared problem through a fictional narrative.
以原创医学剧本，用虚构故事引入共同的问题。

title: Think together
共同推理
text: A diagnostic-themed social game brought discussion and interaction into the activity.
通过诊断主题的社交游戏，让讨论与互动融入活动。

title: Connect with the science
回到科学知识
text: A short educational session connected the experience with tuberculosis prevention knowledge.
通过简短科普，把活动体验连接到结核病预防知识。

role: I designed the interactive health-education event, bringing the story, game and educational session into one coherent experience with the team.
我参与设计这场互动健康教育活动，与团队把故事、游戏和科普环节组织为连贯的体验。
reflection: A familiar activity format can make a technical topic approachable. The event documents an approach to science communication; it was not an evaluation of clinical or educational effectiveness.
熟悉的活动形式，可以让专业议题更容易接近。这场活动体现了健康传播的尝试，并未开展临床效果或教育效果评估。

label: DIALOGUE & WOMEN’S HEALTH
对话与女性健康
title: Make room for difficult questions.
为复杂的问题，留出对话空间。
summary: A student discussion on how pregnancy-related risks, responsibilities and health knowledge should be communicated to the wider public.
一场关于妊娠风险、责任与健康知识应如何向公众传播的学生讨论。
question: What makes health information helpful, balanced and appropriate?
什么样的健康信息，是有帮助、平衡且适当的？
why: Communicating reproductive health involves both medical knowledge and questions about responsibility, audience and personal choice. The discussion made these tensions visible.
生殖健康传播既涉及医学知识，也涉及责任、受众与个人选择。我们通过讨论，让这些需要权衡的问题被看见。

title: Who should know?
向谁普及？
text: Should reproductive risks, responsibilities and possible consequences be discussed with all women, including students and those planning a pregnancy?
是否应向全体女性，包括学生与准备生育的人群，普及生育的风险、责任与可能后果？

title: How much is helpful?
普及到何种程度？
text: When communicating pregnancy-related risks, how much information is helpful, balanced and appropriate?
在传播妊娠风险时，多少信息是有帮助、平衡且适当的？

title: Who shares responsibility?
谁共同参与？
text: Should reproductive-health knowledge form part of public education for both women and men, especially students?
生殖健康知识是否应成为面向女性和男性，尤其是学生的公共教育内容？

role: I facilitated the student discussion, creating space to consider different perspectives on public health communication and medical ethics.
我组织并推动学生讨论，让不同视角围绕健康传播与医学伦理展开交流。
reflection: Facilitation means helping a group examine a question carefully, including where perspectives differ. These prompts are a record of the discussion, not medical advice or a consensus statement.
推动讨论，需要帮助大家认真审视问题，也包括观点分歧之处。这里记录的是讨论议题，并非医学建议或共识声明。

label: PEER VOICES & EXPRESSION
朋辈声音与表达
title: You don’t need to rank first to be heard.
不必名列第一，也值得被听见。
summary: An open sharing platform for students’ learning strategies, social experiences and personal reflections on growth.
一个开放的分享平台，承载学生的学习方法、社会经历与成长思考。
question: Whose experience gets to count as something worth sharing?
什么样的经历，才算值得被分享？
why: A community can hear from a wider range of people when conventional measures of achievement are not the only invitation to speak.
当成绩与传统成就不再是发言的唯一门槛，社群就有机会听见更多人的经验。

title: Share a learning strategy
分享学习方法
text: Students had space to explain ways of learning through their own experience.
为学生留出空间，讲述自己在学习中的实践与方法。

title: Talk about real experience
谈真实经历
text: Social experiences and personal reflections could become material for peer learning.
让社会经历与个人反思，也能成为朋辈学习的内容。

title: Broaden the invitation
拓宽表达的入口
text: The platform welcomed perspectives beyond conventional measures of academic achievement.
欢迎传统学业成绩之外的经验与视角。

role: I created the platform with the community, making room for students to share what they had learned and how they were growing.
我与社群共同搭建这个平台，为学生分享所学、讲述成长留出空间。
reflection: Meaningful engagement can start with a simple invitation: your experience is worth listening to.
有意义的参与，有时就从一个简单的邀请开始：你的经历，值得被倾听。

title: Set the direction
发起与定位
text: Founded Hotwind and helped its purpose evolve from a reading salon into a wider community for dialogue, learning and public engagement.
从零发起热風，推动定位从读书沙龙逐步拓展到对话、学习与公众参与。

title: Listen and adapt
倾听与调整
text: Reflected on the limits of student-led psychological support and helped reposition the project around a more appropriate scope.
反思学生主导心理支持的专业边界，推动项目聚焦更适当的参与范围。

title: Bring the team together
团队与协作
text: Led a nine-member core team, sharing responsibilities and coordinating activities and collaborators over time.
带领9人核心团队，分配职责、协调活动与合作伙伴，让团队持续运转。

title: Turn ideas into experiences
策划与执行
text: Helped develop reading programmes, interactive health communication and open discussions, including the three featured cases.
推动共读、互动健康传播与开放讨论等活动落地，包括网站展示的三个主题案例。
